scenelets.scene: Checking in at the front desk

phrases.es: Tengo una reservación a nombre de...
phrases.en: I have a reservation under the name of...
Is there wifi in the room?

phrases.es: ¿Me puede dar una habitación con vista al mar?
phrases.en: Can I have a room with an ocean view?

scenelets.notes: Hotel front desks in PV are accustomed to English, but Spanish earns warmth and occasional upgrades.

scenelets.scene: Reporting a problem in the room

phrases.en: Can you send someone to check it?
Can I be moved to another room?

scenelets.notes: Use the subjunctive mandar / cambiar forms when making requests — they signal politeness naturally.

phrases.es: Creo que hay un cargo equivocado.
phrases.en: I think there's an incorrect charge.
Can you hold my bag for a few hours?

lines.es: Disculpe, veo un cargo de quinientos pesos que no reconozco.
lines.en: Excuse me, I see a charge of five hundred pesos I don't recognize.

lines.es: Un momento, lo reviso. ¿Fue del minibar?
lines.en: One moment, I'll check. Was it from the minibar?

lines.es: No usé el minibar. Estoy seguro.
lines.en: I didn't use the minibar. I'm sure of it.

lines.es: Tiene razón, fue un error. Lo eliminamos.
lines.en: You're right, it was an error. We'll remove it.

authority_exchange.register_note: Stay confident but not aggressive. 'Estoy seguro' (I'm sure) carries weight without hostility.

register_map.warmth_move: Saying 'muy amables' (so kind) or 'qué buena atención' (great service) to staff creates loyalty for your whole stay.
